body:
[aida:reviewer] #2039 REVIEWED — REQUEST-CHANGES at a2599fe42001, and I had to correct my
own prior finding. 2 of 4 done.

I WAS WRONG ABOUT THE EVIDENCE IN MY EARLIER VERDICT, and I am saying it first because an
implementer would have been sent the wrong way.

My prior F1 said "exactly ONE #[test] appears in the diff, and it is a one-line addition
to an existing lifecycle-transition test". False. The diff adds a dedicated module
bug_1452_refusal_aftermath_tests with a test named
refusal_aftermath_is_parked_held_and_awaiting_visible — named for exactly what criterion
5 asks. The head has not moved (a2599fe420, one commit), so the diff did not change. I
described it incorrectly.

Anyone acting on that finding would have looked for a one-line lifecycle assertion, not
found the real problem, and could reasonably have replied that the test exists.

THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES FOR A BETTER REASON. The test does not test what its name
promises:

    merge_hold::write_hold(root, 1452, "RequestChanges at abc123")   <- called by the test
    shelve_spec_on_failure(root, "BUG-14520", ...)                    <- called by the test
    then asserts the hold exists and the spec is NeedsAttention

It never records a verdict. handle_review_record is never called. So it proves that
write_hold writes a hold and shelve_spec_on_failure shelves a spec — two primitives,
invoked by the test itself — and it would still pass if the recording path stopped
calling either one.

Criterion 5 asks for the aftermath OF A REFUSING VERDICT. This asserts the aftermath of
the test's own two function calls. That is the same shape as the assertion-naming-the-
invariant-it-does-not-enforce problem, and it is a sharper finding than the one I
originally wrote.

F2 UNCHANGED AND BLOCKING: criterion 6's sweep. I grepped the diff for sweep, backfill,
existing-store and report-them language — zero matches across all five changed files. Spec
reads Done, commit carries the (BUG-1452) trailer, so the merge auto-completes it with a
named criterion nobody implemented. Third spec tonight refused for that same shape.

WHAT I KEPT FROM THE PRIOR VERDICT, because my correction does not touch it: criterion 7
is satisfied by construction — the hold is armed inside handle_review_record gated on
kind.blocks_done(), so hand and drain paths are the same code. And write_hold plus
sync_label are both called at refusal, which closes BUG-1499's split-brain source for the
refusal path going forward.

DISCLOSURE CARRIED FORWARD: I argued for criterion 7 today and you promoted it from my
comment. I am independent of the implementation — zero commits from this session — but
not of the spec's scope, and criterion 7 is both the one I am least entitled to judge and
the one I find satisfied. Read it with that attached.

PROVENANCE CLOSED: recorded against a2599fe42001. Second of the five no-sha rows
discharged.

NEXT: #2040, then #2019. #2034's Build is still pending.
subject: #2039 REQUEST-CHANGES at a2599fe42001 — and I corrected my own F1: the aftermath test EXISTS, it just never records a verdict, so it tests two primitives the test itself calls
